note: The spine. Every provider Record Atlas can point at, with what it actually costs to look. `access` is the map's colour and must describe the ordinary visitor's experience, not the best case: FamilySearch is `account` because its images need a free login and some are locked to a Family History Centre. Every row carries `checked`; a row nobody has re-checked in a year should be treated as a claim, not a fact. `at` is where the paper is, or where the portal is run from, at CITY level — a street pin implies a precision that does not survive an institution moving building. A provider with no `at` has no single home: an aggregator, a commercial subscription, or a volunteer index that lives on a server.

access.catalogue: A catalogue entry only — the paper is not photographed

providers.name: FamilySearch
providers.what: The largest free collection of record images and indexes in the world. A free account is required, and a minority of images are restricted to Family History Centres and affiliate libraries.

providers.name: Ancestry
providers.what: The largest commercial collection. Strong on the English-speaking world, censuses and immigration; weak on continental parish registers.

providers.name: MyHeritage
providers.what: Commercial, with a large tree network and good European newspaper and directory coverage. Search is free; opening a record is not.

providers.name: Findmypast
providers.what: Commercial. The strongest British and Irish collection, including parish registers licensed from diocesan archives and the 1921 census of England and Wales.

providers.name: Geneanet
providers.what: Member-contributed trees and transcriptions, strongest in France. Much is free; a Premium tier gates some search and images.

providers.name: Geni
providers.what: One shared world tree. Useful for finding other researchers on the same line; not a record source, and its assertions are only as good as their citations.

providers.name: Find a Grave
providers.what: Volunteer-photographed headstones and cemetery indexes, worldwide, with very uneven coverage. Owned by Ancestry but free to read.

providers.name: BillionGraves
providers.what: GPS-tagged headstone photographs. Smaller than Find a Grave but its coordinates are per-stone, which Find a Grave's often are not.

providers.name: Internet Archive
providers.what: Full-text search across millions of digitised books, including parish histories, nobiliaries and local monographs that name ordinary people.

providers.name: WikiTree
providers.what: A free, single shared tree with an unusually strong sourcing culture. Not a record source.

providers.name: Antenati
providers.what: The Italian state archives' own portal. Civil registration images from 1806, free and without an account — the best national genealogy portal in Europe.

providers.name: Matricula Online
providers.what: Diocesan parish registers photographed and served free, without an account. Austria and much of Germany and Poland; the Italian entries are South Tyrol.

providers.name: Archion
providers.what: The German Protestant church archives' own portal. Subscription by the month; the only route to many Lutheran registers.

providers.name: Arolsen Archives
providers.what: The former International Tracing Service. Concentration camp, forced labour and displaced-persons records for some seventeen and a half million people, free and fully indexed.

providers.name: ANNO — Austrian Newspapers Online
providers.what: The Austrian National Library's digitised newspaper run. Full-text searchable, and it covers the whole empire — which is why it finds Croatian and Istrian names.

providers.name: Hungaricana
providers.what: The Hungarian cultural heritage portal — maps, censuses, urbaria and archival finding aids for the whole Kingdom of Hungary, not today's borders.

providers.name: Szukaj w Archiwach
providers.what: The Polish state archives' scans, free and without an account. Covers ground now in Ukraine, Belarus and Lithuania as well as Poland.

providers.name: Geneteka
providers.what: A volunteer index of Polish parish registers, by surname and parish. An index only — it points you at the scan rather than showing it.

providers.name: Porta fontium
providers.what: A Bavarian–Czech joint portal. Parish registers of western Bohemia, free.

providers.name: Acta Publica
providers.what: Moravian and Silesian parish registers, free. The Czech regional archives each publish their own; this is the Brno one.

providers.name: SIRAnet
providers.what: The Slovenian regional archives' shared catalogue. Largely a finding aid — it tells you the book exists and where it is.

providers.name: dLib.si
providers.what: The Digital Library of Slovenia. Newspapers, journals and books, full-text searchable — and it reaches Istrian and Littoral material.

providers.name: Hrčak
providers.what: The portal of Croatian scientific journals, free and full-text. Local history articles here routinely name and date ordinary families.

providers.name: ARHiNET — Croatian State Archives
providers.what: The Croatian archival network's catalogue. It tells you which archive holds which fonds; the paper itself is almost all in the building.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Pazinu
providers.what: The Pazin State Archive, which holds the parish registers of central Istria. They will search, certify and post a named record for a fee.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Rijeci
providers.what: The Rijeka State Archive — the Kvarner, Fiume's corpus separatum administration, and the Liburnian coast.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Zadru
providers.what: The Zadar State Archive, which holds the Venetian and Austrian registers of Dalmatia — including parishes whose books never went to Split.

providers.name: Archivio di Stato di Udine
providers.what: The Udine state archive — Friuli and Carnia. Its civil registration is published through Antenati; the notarial and estate papers are not.

providers.name: The National Archives — Discovery
providers.what: The catalogue of the UK National Archives and some 2,500 other British archives. The catalogue is free; downloads are often charged.

providers.name: FreeBMD / FreeREG / FreeCEN
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions of English and Welsh civil registration, parish registers and censuses. Free, an index only, and not complete.

providers.name: ScotlandsPeople
providers.what: The official Scottish records — statutory registers, old parish registers, censuses and wills. Pay-per-view credits, and the only lawful route to most of it.

providers.name: IrishGenealogy.ie
providers.what: Irish civil registration images and church records, free and without an account. The single best free national source in these islands.

providers.name: National Library of Ireland — Catholic Parish Registers
providers.what: Every surviving Irish Catholic parish register to 1880, photographed and free. Browse only — no index.

providers.name: Digitalarkivet
providers.what: The Norwegian National Archives, free and largely indexed — censuses, parish registers, emigration lists.

providers.name: Riksarkivet — Digitala forskarsalen
providers.what: The Swedish National Archives. Much is now free; the highest-quality parish register images are on the commercial ArkivDigital.

providers.name: Rigsarkivet — Arkivalieronline
providers.what: The Danish National Archives. Parish registers and censuses, free.

providers.name: Kansallisarkisto / HisKi
providers.what: The Finnish National Archives, plus the Genealogical Society's HisKi parish transcriptions. Free.

providers.name: WieWasWie / Open Archieven
providers.what: The Dutch civil registration indexes, pooled from every regional archive. Free, and unusually complete.

providers.name: Delpher
providers.what: Dutch newspapers, books and periodicals, full-text and free. Death notices here fill gaps the registers leave.

providers.name: PARES
providers.what: The Spanish archives portal — strongest on emigration to the Americas and on military and colonial service.

providers.name: Torre do Tombo / Digitarq
providers.what: The Portuguese national archive's scans, free. District archives publish parish registers through the same system.

providers.name: National Archives Catalog (NARA)
providers.what: The US National Archives catalogue and scans — naturalisations, passenger lists, military service, land.

providers.name: Statue of Liberty–Ellis Island Foundation
providers.what: Passenger arrivals at New York, 1820–1957, with manifest images. Free with an account.

providers.name: Chronicling America
providers.what: The Library of Congress's digitised American newspapers, full-text and free.

providers.name: Library and Archives Canada
providers.what: Canadian censuses, immigration and military service records, free.

providers.name: Trove
providers.what: The National Library of Australia's newspaper archive. Free, full-text, and the single best source for Australian family detail before 1955.

providers.name: National Archives of Australia — RecordSearch
providers.what: Immigration and naturalisation files, service records and alien registration — including the wartime files of European arrivals.

providers.name: Queensland Historical BDM Index
providers.what: Queensland's historical births, deaths and marriages index. Free to search; certificates are charged. Every Australian state runs its own.

providers.name: Archives New Zealand — Collections
providers.what: New Zealand probate, military and immigration records, much of it digitised and free.

providers.name: NAAIRS — National Archives of South Africa
providers.what: The South African archives index — estate files above all, which are the backbone of South African genealogy. An index; the file is ordered from the depot.

providers.name: JewishGen
providers.what: The central Jewish genealogy resource — town-level KehilaLinks, burial and Holocaust databases, and revision lists for eastern Europe.

providers.name: Yad Vashem — Central Database of Shoah Victims' Names
providers.what: Names and testimony pages for victims of the Shoah, free.
